title: Usage credit anchors and automated tier rebalancing: acceptance criteria & billing flows
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Introduce a deterministic 'usage credit anchor' concept and an automated tier rebalancing engine to improve invoice clarity and reduce manual adjustments. Credit anchors are timebound baseline allocations that stabilize burst consumption accounting; rebalancing moves unconsumed committed credit and temporary overage offsets across entitlement tiers at snapshot boundaries. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, billing flows, and edge-case behavior required for the first release of the feature.
background: Customers purchasing committed credits frequently request clearer invoice line items when credits are carried, shifted between teams, or used for short bursts. Current behavior treats credits and overage refunds as isolated events, leading to manual invoice adjustments and support tickets. Engineering has implemented low-level ledger primitives (ENG-33021) to support atomic credit moves; PM needs to define deterministic, auditable policy and UX surfaces so billing and accounting teams can reconcile usage without ad-hoc credits.
goals: Define deterministic rules for 'credit anchors' and transient burst anchors
Implement an automated rebalancing policy that runs at billing snapshot (UTC midnight) and creates audit-friendly ledger entries
Produce acceptance criteria that QA and Finance can validate end-to-end
Surface clear invoice line items and UI explanations in Console billing view
non_goals: Designing a self-serve credit marketplace (out of scope for initial rollout)
Changing existing per-token pricing - pricing changes will be handled separately
Cross-region currency conversion logic (deferred to billing internationalization phase)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A customer with a committed monthly credit bucket (100k tokens) that uses 70k tokens should see 30k moved to a 'carry' anchor at snapshot time with a ledger entry describing source, destination, and timestamp

AC2: A customer with two sub-accounts (project A and B) with per-project anchors - when project A is underutilized and project B bursts, automatic rebalancing should apply carry credits to project B up to the per-plan cap and create a reversible ledger move recorded in the invoice detail
AC3: Invoices must show separate line items for 'Committed Credit Used', 'Anchor Rebalance Moves', and 'Overage Charges' with consistent IDs that map to ledger entries for audit

AC4: Rebalancing respects plan entitlements and hard caps—system must never move credits that would violate contractual caps; attempted moves must result in clear 'insufficient entitlement' ledger entries

AC5: For negative-balance scenarios where automated rebalancing cannot cover overage, system applies configured soft-burst grace window and flags customer for manual review; billing UI surfaces the flag and suggested remediation steps
AC6: All ledger moves related to credit anchors are idempotent and reproducible given the same input snapshot (used for reconciliations and root-cause analysis)

AC7: If a customer's subscription is downgraded mid-cycle, rebalancing runs a pro-rata adjustment that results in a single 'Pro-Rata Reallocation' ledger entry and, if applicable, a prorated invoice credit
AC8: Finance-run reconciliation scripts using the ledger export CSV can compute final owed amount and match it to invoices for all test customers in the QA dataset with 0 discrepancies
AC9: Console billing view exposes a drilldown for each invoice line item to the underlying ledger move ID and the original request IDs (where applicable)
AC10: Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests exist for snapshot creation, rebalancing rules, cap enforcement, and invoice generation; tests are automated in CI with sample datasets
billing_flows: Flow 1 - Normal Month: Snapshot at 00:00 UTC creates baseline anchors -> run rebalancer -> emit ledger moves -> generate invoice line items mapped to moves

Flow 2 - Burst Then Carry: Customer bursts beyond daily cap; system uses transient burst anchor up to configured grace -> at snapshot carry unused committed credit -> ledger entries show transient anchor consumption and subsequent carry
Flow 3 - Downgrade Mid-Cycle: Downgrade event triggers pro-rata reallocation -> a single corrective ledger entry reduces committed credit and generates a credit memo if applicable
Flow 4 - Cross-Project Rebalance: Anchor moves between sub-accounts honor per-project caps and produce a reversible 'transfer' ledger entry
edge_cases: Clock skew between services causing double-application of a move - mitigated by idempotent move IDs and sequence numbers
Late usage ingestion after snapshot - late records are marked as 'post-snapshot' and processed in next cycle with visible flag in invoice detail

Concurrent subscription changes (upgrade + rebalancer run) - deterministic ordering: subscription change -> rebalancer -> invoice; if concurrent, subscription change wins and rebalancer produces a compensating entry
Rounding differences across currencies - reported as a reconciliation delta that Finance must approve; major currency conversions not in scope
Failed ledger write - rebalancer retries with exponential backoff; if persistent failure, system opens a support ticket and flags affected invoices as 'pending reconciliation'
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable rebalancer for 5 opt-in customers with simple single-account setups; Finance runs parallel reconciliation and signs off
Phase 2 (Limited Rollout): Expand to 50 customers including multi-project setups; collect usage patterns and UI feedback
Phase 3 (General Availability): Enable for all new subscriptions; offer backfill for existing customers as a one-time migration with opt-out
Communication: Publish help center article, examples of invoice line items, and a migration FAQ for customers and partners
success_metrics: Reduce manual invoice adjustments related to carried credits by 80% within 60 days of GA
Decrease number of billing support tickets mentioning 'unclear credit movement' by 70% for canary accounts
Ledger/invoice reconciliation match rate >= 99.9% for QA dataset
Average time to produce an auditable invoice post-snapshot under 5 minutes in canary environment
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rebalancer moves credits in ways that surprise customers -> Mitigation: Add verbose console explanations, default opt-in for accounts on first rollout, and a rollback path
Risk: Edge-case rounding causes small negative balances -> Mitigation: Finance tolerance threshold and automatic micro-credit adjustments under configured cap
Risk: Performance impact at snapshot for very large orgs -> Mitigation: Batch processing, sharded rebalancer workers, and concurrency limits; ops run load tests pre-GA
